facts.text: Laurie sits on a ridge that drains in all directions toward the Lake of the Ozarks, giving the town a unique topographic character.
The town’s only historic building, the Laurie Market, was the first in the area to have a telephone and a drilled water well.
During the Great Depression, the completion of Bagnell Dam created the Lake of the Ozarks, turning the surrounding hills into a resort community.
Laurie is located just about two miles north of the Lake of the Ozarks, placing it close to Missouri’s most famous waterway.
Every year from mid‑November to New Year’s Day, Laurie hosts the Enchanted Village of Lights, a drive‑through display that brightens the town for holiday travelers.
The Osage tribe once called the lake area home, and today archaeologists still uncover arrowheads and tomahawks along the Osage River and Gravois Creek.
